title: Article 315: The Commission Behind This Exam

endcard.line: Pictures: unknown (British India) (CC0); IP Singh (public domain)

segments.say: In eighteen fifty-five, the exam for the Indian Civil Service was held only in London.
The first Indian passed in eighteen sixty-four. From nineteen twenty-two, the exam was held in India too. India's first Public Service Commission followed on the first of October nineteen twenty-six.

anim.title: Article 315
items: A Public Service Commission for the Union

segments.say: On the twenty-sixth of January nineteen fifty, it became the UPSC under Article three hundred and fifteen, which also gives each State its own commission.
The President appoints its members, and about half must have served at least ten years under the government. It works from Dholpur House in New Delhi.

anim.title: What it does (Article 320)
items: Conducts exams for the Union services

segments.say: Under Article three hundred and twenty, it conducts the exams, and advises on how to recruit, on promotions, and on disciplinary cases.
The government can reject its advice, but must explain why. The UPSC's yearly report to the President goes before Parliament with a note on each such case.
For GS Two, link the UPSC to Articles three hundred and fifteen to three hundred and twenty-three.

sources: UPSC, About Us, Historical Perspective (upsc.gov.in/about-us): Civil Service Commission set up in London in 1854 and competitive exams started in 1855, initially only in London; first Indian succeeded in 1864; from 1922 the ICS exam was held in India too; the Commission is at Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi; a constitutional body under Article 315

Constitution of India, official English text (Legislative Department diglot PDF, legislative.gov.in, 'as on' 2024 edition): Art. 315 (PSC for the Union and for each State; joint commissions on resolution of the State legislatures); Art. 316 (members appointed by the President; as nearly as may be one-half to have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State); Art. 320 (conducts examinations; consulted on methods of recruitment, principles for appointments, promotions and transfers, disciplinary matters); Art. 323 (annual report to the President, laid before Parliament with a memorandum on cases where advice was not accepted and the reasons)

Wikipedia, 'Union Public Service Commission' (read): established 1 October 1926 as the Public Service Commission; reconstituted as the Federal Public Service Commission by the Government of India Act 1935; constitutional status on 26 January 1950

quiz.q: When was the first Public Service Commission set up in India?
quiz.why: It was set up on 1 October 1926; 1935 brought the Federal PSC.

quiz.q: Under Article 316, roughly how many UPSC members must have ten years in government service?
quiz.why: Art. 316: as nearly as may be one-half.

quiz.q: What happens when the government doesn't accept UPSC advice?
options: The case is explained in a memo laid before Parliament
The UPSC can overrule the government
quiz.why: Art. 323: a memorandum explains each such case and the reasons.
